subject: Problem with fitting proportional hazard model with INLA

messages.author: e803483734a6a2a7
messages.subject: Problem with fitting proportional hazard model with INLA
parts:
Hello,

I am following code from Alvares et al. 2024's publication to fit a proportional hazards model:

R> m2.pwc <- joint(formSurv = inla.surv(time = time, event = delta) ~ stage + age + diagyr, + basRisk = "rw1", NbasRisk = 3, dataSurv = larynx) 

The error I'm receiving is:
Error in joint(surv ~ trt, data = times, basRisk = "rw1", NbasRisk = 3) : could not find function "joint"
I've updated the INLA package and it says I am up to date. I've also loaded the package and can fit a AFT model with inla.surv(). I'd appreciate troubleshooting this issue, thank you. 

Best,
Andrew

messages.author: 953deaf1a512b96e
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem with fitting proportional hazard model with INLA
parts:
Hi,

Since INLAjoint is handling both longitudinal and survival models, you need to set 'dataSurv' instead of 'data' as the second argument name, to avoid confusion with the alternative (dataLong). Also I suggest to remove 'NbasRisk=3' as the default is 15 which will be more accurate.

Best,
Denis Rustand

parts:
Apologies if this is obvious, but how do we check prior specification of the fitted model (I want to check if I've specified it correctly)? And how do we set priors for multiple covariates? 

My current code: 
#specifying prior
priorinfo<-list(mean=0,prec=2,mean.intercept=0,prec.intercept=2)
#setting up the response variable
surv<-inla.surv(times$eventtime,times$status)
#aft model specification
inlamod1<-joint(surv~trt,dataSurv=times,basRisk="weibullsurv",control=list(priorFixed=priorinfo))
